hyperedges.label: Four field-family controls built from one PCF project
Build, version bump and solution packaging pipeline

nodes.label: Single PCF Project (FieldReview.pcfproj)
nodes.rationale: All four controls always build together from one project; one solution reference brings in all four controls.

nodes.label: One-step build (build.cmd)
nodes.rationale: Recommended path: npm build, then version bump, then dotnet package. Stops before touching versions if the build fails.

nodes.label: Control and Solution Version Bumping
nodes.rationale: Dataverse may keep serving the cached older bundle unless the control manifest version increases before each import or push; build.cmd bumps automatically, pac pcf push does not.

nodes.label: Package into Dataverse Solution
nodes.rationale: Solution lives in its own Solution/ folder because the repo root is the PCF project itself.

nodes.label: Managed vs Unmanaged Solution (SolutionPackageType)
nodes.rationale: Managed is right for test/production: cannot be edited in target and deletes cleanly. Do not import over an unmanaged copy, which sits on top and keeps winning.

nodes.label: Quick deploy with pac pcf push
nodes.norm_label: quick deploy with pac pcf push

nodes.label: skipBuildLinting in pcfconfig.json
nodes.rationale: Build-time ESLint is off because the project ships no ESLint config; add eslint.config.mjs and remove the flag to lint.

nodes.label: Local test harness (npm start watch)
nodes.rationale: Shows only the first control and is not connected to Dataverse, so comment threads and lookup records do not load.

nodes.label: Field comment/assignment thread
nodes.rationale: Each comment is open until any one assignee resolves it, resolving it for everyone; full history visible to all.

nodes.label: One control per field family
nodes.rationale: A bound property declares one type-group; mixing Lookup.Simple or OptionSet with scalar types is undocumented and pcf-scripts falls back to untyped Property, so rather than gamble on runtime binding, ship one control per family from a single project.

nodes.label: FieldReviewPolyLookupControl
nodes.rationale: Bound to a text column that hosts the control and names the review thread; the selection itself lives in a relationship saved immediately via Web API.

nodes.label: Shared dropdown (common/dropdown.ts)
nodes.rationale: Lookup and Choice controls render with the same dropdown so both field types look and behave the same.

nodes.label: Shared common/ folder
nodes.rationale: One copy of settings parsing, Web API calls, panel UI and pickers; webpack bundles it into each control's bundle.js separately.

nodes.label: Review settings (JSON)
nodes.rationale: Nothing about table/column naming is hardcoded, so the same compiled control works across environments and publisher prefixes.

nodes.label: regardingMode (text vs lookup)
nodes.rationale: Text mode: one comment table serves any parent with no schema change, but no clickable link, subgrid or cascade delete. Lookup mode restores those at the cost of one Lookup column per parent table.

nodes.label: Create-form selection via JSON + post-operation plugin
nodes.rationale: Records cannot be related before the current record exists; JSON output in DCE PolyLookup shape lets a Create plugin make the associations.
nodes.norm_label: create-form selection via json + post-operation plugin

nodes.label: Assignment table (insurgo_reviewassignment)
nodes.rationale: Only records who is assigned to which comment, one row per person; has no status of its own.

nodes.label: Migration from per-assignee status to comment status
nodes.rationale: Control refuses to load while old assignmentStatus* keys remain so an outdated config cannot go unnoticed.
nodes.norm_label: migration from per-assignee status to comment status

nodes.label: Current record detection via context.mode.contextInfo
nodes.rationale: Undocumented for field-bound controls but a long-standing community workaround; URL parsing is the fragile last-resort fallback.

nodes.label: Table metadata via context.utils.getEntityMetadata
nodes.rationale: Reads EntitySetName, PrimaryIdAttribute, PrimaryNameAttribute; PrimaryIdAttribute matters for activity tables (activityid not taskid).

nodes.label: Lookup navigation property resolution
nodes.rationale: @odata.bind requires the case-sensitive navigation property, often not the logical name; read from relationship metadata via direct Web API, fallback to logical name with *NavigationProperty overrides.

nodes.label: Multi-target lookup forces native search dialog
nodes.rationale: Merging candidates from several tables in one dropdown is a bigger feature than this control takes on.
nodes.norm_label: multi-target lookup forces native search dialog

nodes.label: Clearing value via undefined from getOutputs
nodes.norm_label: clearing value via undefined from getoutputs

nodes.label: Direct Web API calls for metadata and N:N $ref
nodes.rationale: PCF webAPI cannot query metadata or associate/disassociate, so same-origin fetch calls are used.
nodes.norm_label: direct web api calls for metadata and n:n $ref

nodes.label: Not built yet (assignment notification, field state, view search)
nodes.rationale: Assignment notification deliberately out of scope: needs a plugin or Power Automate flow.
nodes.norm_label: not built yet (assignment notification, field state, view search)
